note: A fictional conversation written for the replay (specs/together.md §11.3): the Lakeshore QA copy's broker (Morgan) and owner (Tony). Nothing here is a real person or a real business.
deal: QA OCT — Lakeshore Home Comfort Ltd.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Thanks for making the time, Tony. This should take about half an hour.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: No problem. Denise put the coffee on.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Let's start with the year. Tell me about the busy and the quiet months.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Summer and the cold snaps are crazy. June through August, then December to February.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: April and October are dead, we do maintenance and catch up on paperwork.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: And who keeps the dispatch board running day to day.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Denise runs dispatch on our field service software, and I jump in when it gets busy.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: The techs see their jobs on their phones, customers get a text when the van is on the way.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: How crazy does a July day get?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: In July we can run a hundred and twenty calls a day.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: What do you do yourself in a normal week?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: I'm in the office three days, four in busy season. I do the quotes on Mondays and run the Friday tech meeting.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Hmm, let me think.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: And I still do the big commercial estimates myself, nobody else touches those.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: How many people are on the team now?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: About forty. Actually thirty-eight, counting the two part-time girls in the office.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: How many members are in the Comfort Club these days?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Just under three thousand, about twenty-nine hundred.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: So they renew at about eighty-five percent a year?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Yeah, that's right.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: What's the safety rating with WSIB, the EMR?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: My bookkeeper Denise has the EMR, I'd have to ask her.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: No problem, we'll get it from her.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: So the weather today, can you believe this rain?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Good for the furnace business, I'll tell you that.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: What's prompting the sale now?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Thirty years is enough. I'm sixty-four and the wife wants Florida.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: I had a heart scare last spring, that's part of it too. Keep the health stuff out of the book, eh?

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Of course, that stays between us.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: And Dave asked me about buying in, he's been with me sixteen years. I don't know what to tell him.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Let's talk about that one separately.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Your lease runs to August 2028, I saw that in the file.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Okay, moving on to where the business could go next.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: If you had more time or money, where would you grow it?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Heat pumps, for sure. The rebates made them about a fifth of our installs already.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: And it keeps climbing every quarter since the rebate program started.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: People call asking for them now, we used to have to sell them.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: We could open a second location up in Barrie too.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Half our calls from up there already come from cottagers in the summer.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: A small shop with two vans would pay for itself in a couple of years.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Commercial maintenance contracts are the other one.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Strip plazas and small offices, rooftop units, that kind of thing.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Steady money all year, and you book it in the slow months.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: We have maybe a dozen of those now and never went after more.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: And a proper second install crew.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: We turn down jobs every July because we only have the one crew.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: That's real money walking out the door every summer.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: The trucks are there, it's finding the right lead installer.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Honestly I never had the time to chase any of it.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: I'm still on the tools half the week, so it just never happens.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Marketing too, we've never spent a dime on ads, it's all referrals.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Our reviews are good, people find us on their own.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: A younger owner with some energy could double the commercial side.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Maybe in three years if they push it.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: And the Comfort Club could be bigger, we never push it at installs.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Every install should leave with a membership, but the guys forget.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: A simple process fixes that, a checkbox on the work order.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: So there's a lot of upside, I'm just the wrong guy to chase it now.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: That's about it really.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Oh, and duct cleaning, we sub that out and could bring it in-house.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: That's a nice little add-on for the slow months too.

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Anyway, that's the list.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: What's the gross margin like on service versus installs?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Service runs about fifty percent, installs closer to thirty-five.
Avg service call ticket about $375

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: What are you known for with customers?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: We're the no-surprise pricing people. Flat rates, posted on the website, no upsell games.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Who would you want to take it over?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Someone who'll treat the guys right. Not a private equity roll-up that guts the team.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Would you stay on to help the new owner?

lines.speaker: dg:1
lines.text: Six months, longer if they need it. I'd do the commercial estimates and introduce them to the builders.

lines.speaker: dg:0
lines.text: Great, thank you, that's a lot covered.
